newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Barshefsky says unclear if EU wants infotech deal.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky says unclear if EU wants infotech deal.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Thursday expressed concern about whether the European Union wants to complete a deal to liberalise trade in information technology by the conclusion of this week's World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting.
Barshefsky said to reporters following a speech to the American Chamber of Commerce here that "it is not at this point clear to me whether the European Union will move forward or not."
"The outcome of the European Council deliberations will tell the story of the EU's commitment to the ITA and thus its commitment to further trade liberalisation," Barshefsky said.

Barshefsky and the European Trade Commission Sir Leon Brittan met early on Thursday morning as the two sides continued an intense effort to resolve their differences on an information technology agreement that would eliminate tariffs on a wide range of computer and telecommunications products by 2000.
In her talk to the American Chamber of Commerce, Barshefsky said "the European Union has not yet decided what it wants to do apparently."
She told reporters later that she still hoped to have an agreement on information technology trade by the close of the first ministerial meeting on Friday.
She said she hoped that the European Union would move forward, adding that "plainly an agreement is in their interest as it is in the interest of the WTO and trade liberalisation."
